FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: It's a position we've earned over three decades and one we are strengthening every day. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: During Q3, a large energy and utilities provider with more than 1,000 mission-critical applications running on F5 expanded its footprint significantly in a major overhaul of its cloud infrastructure across three regions and multiple data centers. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: In an example that highlights both a competitive displacement and an AI data delivery win, we displaced an incumbent at a Fortune 100 global enterprise technology provider. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: During Q3, a multi-brand telecommunications provider replaced a fragmented collection of security tools with F5 Distributed Cloud Services. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: Following a competitive evaluation, F5 Distributed Cloud Services displaced the incumbent, providing web application and API protection, DDoS mitigation, and bot defense on a unified platform. Since deployment, threats that previously evaded detection are now being identified and blocked.

FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: This foundation can be extended to every new environment they deploy, mitigating both agentic and traditional bot attacks. Finally, the AI inference inflection is driving demand for F5, both indirectly as customers expand hybrid multi-cloud deployments, and directly through our three AI use cases, AI data delivery, AI runtime security, and AI factory load balancing. Momentum is building across all three. In fact, our cumulative total customer count for direct AI use cases grew 50% just in Q3, underscoring the accelerating pace of demand.

FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: A few notable wins from the quarter illustrate our traction. In AI data delivery, we are accelerating secure AI data pipelines, ensuring storage, networking, and data delivery and keeping AI clusters fully utilized across hybrid and multi-cloud deployments. With exploding data volumes and throughput demand, the customer needed additional capacity. F5 outperformed the competitor, simplifying connectivity and storage sharing across their data centers, and expanding our role as the trusted traffic layer between storage and compute.

FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: In AI runtime security, we are safeguarding AI applications, APIs, and models from abuse, data leaks, and attacks like prompt injection. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: In AI factory load balancing, we are optimizing traffic and GPU utilization both across and within AI factories, increasing token throughput, reducing time to first token, and lowering per-token costs. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: That's exactly why we are innovating to lead the next generation of capabilities and get them deployed with customers faster so they are ready as requirements intensify. FranÃ§ois Locoh-Donou Chairman, President, and CEO at F5: This is how F5 is turning the disruption created by frontier AI into stronger security and greater resilience for our customers. Now, I will turn the call over to Cooper, who will walk through our Q3 results and our outlook. Cooper?

Cooper Werner EVP and CFO at F5: We continue to expect mid-single-digit software revenue growth, double-digit systems revenue growth, and low single-digit services revenue growth for the year. key_takeaways.texte: F5 reported strong Q3 execution, with revenue up 11% to $865 million, product revenue up 19%, systems revenue up 32%, and non-GAAP EPS up 14% to $4.73.
The company raised its fiscal 2026 outlook, now expecting revenue growth of approximately 9%–10% versus prior guidance of 7%–8%, and non-GAAP EPS of $17.21–$17.33 versus $16.25–$16.55 previously.

AI-related momentum is accelerating across data delivery, runtime security, and AI-factory load balancing; direct AI-use-case customers grew 50% in Q3, while AI-security customers doubled during the quarter.

Management cited durable demand from hybrid multi-cloud adoption, digital sovereignty, competitive displacements, platform consolidation, and rising application-layer threats, supporting continued hardware expansion and an expected return to solid double-digit software growth in fiscal 2027.

Management acknowledged that part of the 32% systems growth is tied to the cyclical iSeries refresh, and maintained fiscal 2027 gross-margin guidance of 80%–82% because memory and storage component pricing remains uncertain.
